A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PI-MDP and partially equivariant reinforcement-learning work. All 27 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PE-DQN and PE-SAC experiments on Grid-World, locomotion and manipulation, with ablations in Appendix C and an error-propagation analysis in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations and error-propagation analysis.

M1.justification: The PI-MDP construction, predictor-disagreement supervision, gated critics, actor gates and PE-DQN/PE-SAC objectives remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 combines two gate-update lines without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Grid-World obstacle, reward-penalty and stochastic-transition scenarios, plus Hopper, Ant, Swimmer, Fetch Reach and UR5e Reach. The rewritten experimental overview does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain vanilla RL, exact-equivariant RL, RPP and Approximately Equivariant RL. Park et al. changes from a 2024 preprint citation to its 2025 publication; Appendix D retains the same baseline adaptation.

E3.justification: Observations, environment perturbations, metrics and hyperparameters are unchanged. Figures 3–5 retain training budgets of 100K steps for Grid-World, 1M for locomotion, 30K for Fetch and 500K for UR5e.

E4.justification: Both retain the reward/stochastic Grid-World tests, actor-gating alternatives, hard/soft gating, network-sharing and threshold-sensitivity ablations, and equivariance-error case study in Figures 4 and 6–10.

E5.justification: Both report standard errors over eight seeds for locomotion and five for Grid-World and manipulation, with five seeds for Appendix C ablations. Although v2 removes a redundant setup sentence, the figure captions preserve the statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 3–10 retain the same result curves, uncertainty bands, ablation outcomes and error visualization. Their associated findings are unchanged; no result entries are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 corrects an inconsistent formula: v1 recalls delta as epsilon_R + 2 gamma Vmax, omitting epsilon_P. v2 instead references the correct definition in Eq. (2), already present unnumbered in v1. Other bound revisions use equivalent notation; the theoretical guarantees remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: analyzing propagated symmetry-breaking errors, introducing PI-MDP and selective gating, and demonstrating sample efficiency and robustness with PE-DQN and PE-SAC.

C2.justification: The explanations of benchmark behavior and applicability limits remain unchanged. The rewritten conclusion retains computational overhead and limited benefit under pervasive symmetry-breaking, where routing largely defaults to unconstrained networks.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link to the abstract. Implementation details, hardware and hyperparameters in Appendices B and D remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish what code or data the linked page provides.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Chang et al. (2026), Group-invariant unsupervised skill discovery. The central positioning against global equivariance relaxation remains unchanged. Other citation-year and venue updates generally refer to the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: v2 condenses related-work examples, preliminaries and explanatory prose, rewrites the experimental overview and conclusion, and updates terminology, bibliographic formatting and the publication header. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives a rewritten caption explicitly distinguishing the two agents' valid and blocked rotated actions. Algorithm 1 is slightly compressed, and text reflows so the conclusion fits on page 10. Figure graphics and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes the inconsistent formula in Appendix A.2 and makes Figure 1's caption better match the illustrated actions. The project-page link and prose/reference cleanup provide additional modest usability gains. The method, experimental evidence and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
